Interacting with Reality

What can a person do once objects, places and people have a digital counterpart?
An HCI-first research atlas: interaction techniques and systems, not a catalogue of computer-vision models.

Open editable lecture slides ↗Download slide PDF ↗CPU mini-lab
Different from last week: RealitySketch, AniCraft, RealityCanvas and Teachable Reality were already in the previous lecture. New examples are prioritized here. “Visual Responsiveness” is interpreted as Scene Responsiveness, the exact title recovered from the existing course showcase.

Four research categories

01 · Object Tracking

Recognize, locate, query and interact with real objects. NaviCam introduces the historical thread.

02 · Avatar

Capture and represent people for shared presence, collaboration and contextual avatar instruction.

03 · Digital Twin

Capture, edit and remix environments. Urp provides a historical simulation example.

04 · 3D Generation

Author and generate 3D content, from Teddy's sketches to contemporary generative systems.

Compare the human control point

A detector can tell us where an object is. HCI asks what people should be able to do through it. Compare input → representation → human control → outcome. A scan, a live reconstruction, an IoT-state twin and a generated scene are not interchangeable. Research hardware and GPU requirements are recorded in each paper's details; these are not claims of newly verified Quest ports.
